verdict.rationale: dlt is an open-source Python library: pipelines are ordinary Python code plus declarative configuration that runs wherever Python runs. Destinations can be switched without changing pipeline code, and a community user confirms that doing 'everything via code' makes pipelines more maintainable. Code in a repository is inherently versionable and reviewable, and the GitHub Actions deployment guide fits that repo-centric workflow. Missing for 10: explicit first-party documentation of a git-based versioning and code-review workflow for pipeline projects (implied, not described).

support.subject: As a data engineer, my pipelines are plain code and config in my own repository — versioned, reviewed, and portable like any software

citations.quote: dlt is an open-source Python library that loads data from various, often messy data sources into well-structured datasets.
Write the pipeline in Python and run it wherever Python already runs: a laptop, a notebook, Airflow, Dagster, a Lambda, a container.
This approach is especially useful when switching between destinations without modifying the actual pipeline code.
Using a declarative configuration, you can define: the API endpoints to pull data from, their relationships, how to handle pagination, authentication.
try the GitHub Actions guide which has a generous free tier for anyone using GitHub
One of the reasons why I like dlt is because I can do everything via code, which makes things more maintainable, for me.
